title: About Me
text:
My Hometown
I grew up in Manhattan Beach, California, which is also more casually known as “The Bubble”! I grew up just a few blocks up from the beach, which is what brought me to love the ocean and inspired me to potentially pursue a career in marine conservation. I will forever love my hometown and am so grateful to have gotten to grow up in such a beautiful place.

title: About Me
text:
My Family






In order left to right: Brother (Marty), Mom, Me, Dad





I grew up in a very loving, supportive family with my mom (Zoya), dad (John) and my little brother Marty (3 years younger). My family is super important to me and they are the reason I am who I am today. Without my mom, I would not know what hard work and dedication was. Without my dad, I would not know what empathy was, or be as caring for others as I am today. Without my brother, I would have been bored out of my mind during COVID, and would not have a soft and loving spot in my heart. One day, I hope to be as fun and hardworking as my parents are. Some of our favorite family activities include playing cards, surfing, road tripping, and binge watching SNL skits while dying laughing.

The Family Password: Pepper






Pepperoncini Cocoa Matich: our lovely Bernese Mountain Dog





Pepper is the love of my life and the best dog in the entire world. She was the topic of my college personal statement essay, which got me in to so many schools, and is our cherished COVID baby. She is also known as: Boom, Booming, Mamas, Peps, Pepsi, and more.

title: About Me
text:
Education + Aspirations
I currently have a focus in Marine Biology and Terrestrial ecology. Some of my career interests are field work and getting involved in marine or terrestrial conservation and restoration work. I am very passionate about sustainability and protecting our natural resources and species
Some upcoming exciting news is that I will be participating in the Bren Fellowship Program this upcoming summer assisting on the “Promoting Wildfire Resilience in Santa Barbara County” project. I was also selected to be published in the 2026 Edition of Starting Lines, the text book for the UCSB writing program.

title: Ostional, Costa Rica
text:
The summer in between my Freshman Sophomore year of college (2024), I signed up to go on the 10 day sea turtle field course in Ostional, Costa Rica. Here, I gained valuable experience in field work, data collection and learned a lot about local conservation management strategies around the Olive Ridley Sea Turtle species. Data collection consisted of night patrols from 8pm-12am or 12am-4am where we counted turtle abundance, measured the turtle, clutch size, counted the number of eggs laid and the time it took to do so.




During my time in Ostional, I got to witness an arribada (mass nesting event), which took place across 3 days. Here we saw thousands on female turtles come up the beach to nest. I will forever cherish this experience and it is what has encouraged me to get involved in species conservation and take the ENVS 193ST: Sea Turtle Conservation and Management course at UCSB.

On this map is my guide of everywhere we went and everywhere we saw! Truly an adventure of a lifetime.

title: New Zealand
text:
Some Quick Photo Highlights






Rob Roys Glacial Track: My favorite hike we did! Absolutely stunning with a glacial view at the end.







Tasman Glaciar Track: One of the first and easiest hikes we did along a glacier. Our first stop on our road trip







Roys Peak: Longest, hardest, most rewarding hike we did. We woke up at 2 am and began the hike at 2:30am to get to the peak for sunrise.

title: Does harbor activity influence Tridacna maxima giant clam size, density and population dynamics on Heron Island?
text: For my study abroad Marine Biology field course in teh Fall 2025, I went through the entire research process, where in groups we developed a research question and project outline studying Giant Clam ecology in Heron Island. Our group analyzed the differences in size and abundance across a disturbed (near by the island harbor) and undisturbed site on the island.

title: A Translation on Anotation
text:
As my Writing 2 Project 2 in Spring 2025, I developed a podcast script that resembled a conversation between different peer reviewed articles and authors. The topic of interest was the benefit and the downfalls of annotation in preliminary education. As of this past May, this project will be published in the 2026 Edition of Starting Lines, the text book for Writing 1, Writing 2, and Linguistics 3A, 3B, 3C classes
